newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Coles Myer says sells A$558 mln assets.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Coles Myer says sells A$558 mln assets.

text.p: Australian retailer Coles Myer Ltd said on Monday it had sold A$558 million worth of property assets to a range of investors.
Earlier, property group Westfield Trust revealed itself as one of the buyers, purchasing shopping centres in Bisbane and Perth for a total A$185 million.

The sales also included the Roselands shopping centre in Sydney to a group of private investors and and the group's half stakes in Melbourne's Eastland shopping centre and the Toowoomba shopping centre redevelopment to Queensland Investment Corp.
"These transactions bring the total in property sales by Coles Myer to around A$830 million since July 1996, sold at a combined premium to book value," Coles said.
About A$705 million will be settled by the end of the first half of this financial year to January 26, 1997, it added.
The A$558 million also included the sale of five neighbourhood shopping centres to MCS Asset Management.
The proceeds will be used in the short term to retire debt, lowering the group's gearing ratio to within its target range of between 55 and 60 percent, Coles Myer said.

"This will allow future investment to concentrate on appropriate retail assets, which generate higher returns than those available on property," Coles Myer chief executive Peter Bartels said in a statement.
Bartels also announced the group had reached agreement for the exit of its six World 4 Kids stores in Westfield shopping centres over the next 18 months.
"Today's announcement is a major achievement for the company," he said in a statement.
"It is part of our long-term strategy to focus on core retail operations and to more effectively manage our assets and balance sheet."

He estimated that Coles Myer now had about A$400 million in property assets left on its books, but they were mainly under development or heritage-listed sites and would be seen as strategic. "They're the flagship sites," Burgess added.

Both Burgess and J.B. Were analyst George Batsakis agreed the sales, and the closure of six World 4 Kids stores, were more positive signs that Coles was making progress in turning around its recent poor performance.
"Yes. They are making progress," Batsakis said.
